reasoning_quality_informational.v1_root_problem: Billing dispute tickets doubled from ~600/month (Jun-Jul 2026) to ~1200+/month (Aug-Sep 2026) (E-05). Field manual-read route completion fell to 88% against a 95% target in that same window (E-01, 9200 accounts), triggering the meter-to-cash estimate-substitution step and producing estimated bills that account for the 1240 ESTIMATED-read disputed bills in E-02 — but not the larger 1785 ACTUAL-read disputed-bill share, whose cause current evidence does not establish.
reasoning_quality_informational.v2_root_problem: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled from ~600/month (Jun-Jul 2026) to ~1200+/month (Aug-Sep 2026) (E-05). Of 3025 disputed bills, the 1240 ESTIMATED-read ones (E-02) are entirely AMI-channel reads (E-10); 1184 of those (95.5%) were valid AMI reads received before cutoff and exported to billing but rejected as REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION (E-10). This rejection is produced by billing validation rule BV-17, deployed 2026-08-01, which compares the raw AMI register value directly against 12-month m3 history with no unit_scaling (E-12), while meter firmware v4.2 (rollout 2026-06) reports register values in units of 0.1 m3 instead of m3 (E-11) — making a normal reading appear ~10x inflated, triggering rejection, and forcing estimate substitution that mismatches true consumption and drives disputes for this subset.
reasoning_quality_informational.ideal_final_problem: BV-17 validation rejects valid firmware-v4.2 AMI reads (unit-scale mismatch on H-MDMS-BILL) and substitutes estimates.
